class.name: NetwClockHandle
class.brief_description: The tick every peer in the session counts, reached by [method Netw.clock].
class.description:
A tick is a numbered step of the simulation. Every peer counts the same ticks, and a client keeps its count in step with the server's. [member tick] is the number every [NetwRecord] and lag compensation uses. [codeblock] var c := Netw.clock(self) c.before_tick.connect(sample_input) c.on_tick.connect(step) label.text = "tick %d" % c.tick [/codeblock]
[b]How a tick is produced[/b] Each physics frame adds its delta to an accumulator, and every [code]1 / tickrate[/code] seconds in it runs one tick. A slow frame can run two ticks and a fast one none. At a [member tickrate] of 30 with 60 physics ticks per second, a tick runs every second frame, and [member physics_factor] is [code]2.0[/code]. At most [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME] ticks run in one frame. [member behind_count] counts how often that limit was hit.
[b]How a client follows the server[/b] The client pings the server every [member ping_interval] seconds. The server answers with its tick, and the client aims ahead of it by half the round trip plus [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_LEAD_TICKS]. The first answer sets the tick directly. After that, [member sync_mode] decides. [constant NetwMultiplayer.SYNC_MODE_SNAP] sets the tick directly every time, which can move it backwards. [constant NetwMultiplayer.SYNC_MODE_STRETCH], the default, runs the clock slightly faster or slower each frame by [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_STRETCH_NUDGE_FACTOR] of the difference, so the tick never jumps. A difference larger than [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_PANIC_SNAP_THRESHOLD] ticks is snapped.
[b]Showing remote state[/b] State from other peers arrives late, so remote entities are shown [member display_offset] ticks in the past. [member recommended_display_offset] is the offset the current connection needs, the one-way latency plus the jitter times [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_JITTER_MULTIPLIER], in ticks. It is not applied automatically. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_auto_configure_offset] applies it.

method.name: monitor
method.description: Returns one clock diagnostic value. [codeblock] var rtt := Netw.clock(self).monitor(NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_MONITOR_RTT_AVG) [/codeblock]

members.member: How many frames could not run every tick they needed. If it keeps growing, this machine is too slow for [member tickrate].
How many ticks in the past remote entities are shown. See [member recommended_display_offset].
[code]true[/code] once the settings from [method Netw.configure_clock] are applied. [member tick] does not move before that.
[code]true[/code] once the tick follows the server. Always [code]true[/code] on the server.
Physics frames per tick. Multiply a per-frame value by it to get a per-tick value.
Seconds between pings. Shorter follows the connection more closely and sends more packets.
The [member display_offset] the current connection needs, in ticks. Not applied automatically.
How the tick is corrected toward the server's.
How far time has moved past the last tick, as a fraction of a tick. Use it to interpolate.
How far into the current tick the clock is, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].
Ticks per second, set by [method Netw.configure_clock]. The same on every peer.

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Emitted before [param tick] runs. Read input here.

signal.name: on_tick
signal.description: Emitted when [param tick] runs. Run game logic here.
